draft.title: Add `ledger report trial-balance` to the CLI
draft.why: Accountants closing a period fetch the trial balance from the HTTP API with curl and paste it into a spreadsheet. The CLI they already use for `ledger close` has no report command, so the close checklist mixes two tools and two logins.
draft.what:
The Ledger CLI (`src/ledger/cli.py`) gains `ledger report trial-balance --period <YYYY-MM> [--tenant T] [--json]`. It calls the existing reporting service, which reads `v_trial_balance` through the Postgres store. No SQL is added outside `src/ledger/storage/postgres.py`.

Plain output is one line per account: account, debit and credit in minor units. `--json` prints the same object `GET /v1/reports/trial-balance` returns.

Out of scope: no new report types and no change to the HTTP API.

### Behaviour

`ledger report trial-balance --period 2026-08` prints the accounts of that period with their balances and exits 0. An unknown period exits 2 with `error: period 2026-13 not found` on stderr.
acceptance: `ledger report trial-balance --period 2026-08 --json` prints the same JSON as `GET /v1/reports/trial-balance?period=2026-08` for the test tenant.
`ledger report trial-balance --period 2026-13` exits 2 and prints `error: period 2026-13 not found` on stderr.
`test_cli.py::test_report_trial_balance` passes and asserts that no query touches the `entries` table.
context: Reports read from the reporting views (`v_trial_balance`), never from the entries table.
The Ledger CLI is a thin wrapper over the same services the API router calls; `--json` mirrors the API shapes.
The HTTP API serves `/v1/reports/<name>` through the API router.

components.name: API router
components.provides: Maps HTTP routes to service calls and turns service errors into JSON error responses.

components.name: Auth
components.provides: Session cookie and API token authentication as router middleware; loads the current tenant.

components.name: Cache helper
components.provides: A TTL cache in front of Postgres store reads, keyed by query name and parameters, invalidated on every write through post_entry.
components.interface: get(key) -> value | None; set(key, value, ttl_s=60); invalidate(prefix)

components.name: CSV importer
components.provides: Parses bank statement CSV files into candidate entries and posts them through post_entry after matching rules.

components.name: Event bus
components.provides: An in-process publish/subscribe bus for audit, email and webhook side effects, drained after each request.

components.name: Invoice renderer
components.provides: Renders invoices to HTML and PDF from a period's entries using server-side templates.

components.name: Ledger CLI
components.provides: Command-line entry point for posting entries, closing periods and running imports against a local or remote Ledger.

components.name: Postgres store
components.provides: All SQL for entries, periods, tenants and reporting views; the only module that opens a database connection.

decisions.title: ADR 0001: Postgres over SQLite
decisions.decision: Ledger uses one Postgres database with a tenant column on every table and reporting views per tenant; SQLite is dropped, including for tests.
alternatives: SQLite file per tenant: no concurrent writers and no shared reporting.
Redis as a cache tier: rejected in favour of the in-process Cache helper to keep one runtime dependency.

decisions.title: ADR 0002: Server-rendered invoices
decisions.decision: Invoices are rendered on the server to HTML and PDF by the Invoice renderer; there is no client-side invoice template.
alternatives: A JavaScript front end rendering invoices from the JSON API: rejected because PDFs must match the HTML byte for byte.
A third-party invoicing SaaS: rejected on data residency.

decisions.title: ADR 0003: Event bus for audit and email
decisions.decision: Audit records and outbound email are produced by subscribers on the in-process Event bus, drained after commit; services never call the mailer or the audit table directly.
alternatives: Inline calls from each service: rejected because every service would need the mailer and audit dependencies.
A message broker such as RabbitMQ: rejected as infrastructure the deployment does not have.
